children.value: Interactive map of crime counts and rates of Greater Sydney

children.label: Interactive map of crime counts and rates of Greater Sydney

children.value: Overall, crime counts tend to be lower in the northern LGAs, while higher counts are observed across southern and western LGAs. This spatial pattern is consistent across all three crime categories.
A similar pattern is evident in crime rates, with northern LGAs generally recording lower rates than those in the southern and western parts of the study area.
Sydney LGA presents the highest crime count for drug offences
Blacktown LGA presents the highest crime count for violent crime and property offences, However, Sydney LGA presnts the highest crime rate for all crime types
Interactive crime trends map of Greater Sydney

children.label: Interactive crime trends map of Greater Sydney

children.value: Blacktown, Paramatta and Burwood all have increasing drug offences over time. All other LGA’s have decreasing drug offences or no correlation over time
Majority of LGA’s, except Sydney, Hunters Hill, Mosman and North Sydney, have increasing violent crime over time
Majority of LGA’s, except Strathfield, Camden, Parramatta, Ryde and Lane Cove, have decreasing property offences over time
Interactive crime hotspot map of Greater Sydney

children.label: Interactive crime hotspot map of Greater Sydney

children.value: Across all crime categories cold spots were identifyied on North Eastern LGA’s. This includes Northern Beaches, Ku-ring-ga and Willoughby
No hotpsots were identified on the North Shore
Woollahra was identified as a hotspot for all three crime types
Drug Offence hotspots were idenitified in Woollahra, Randwick and Bayside
Violent Crime hotspots were idenitified in Fairfield and Woollahra
Property Offence hotspots were identified in Randwick and Woollahra
Note: Some scatter plots in this section have a line of best fit. This is to highlight the direction of correlation.
Graph 1: Example Data with Sydney LGA

children.label: Graph 1: Example Data with Sydney LGA

children.value: This graph displays the relationship between property offences and year 12 completion. Sydney (labelled) stands out as an obvious outlier. This relationship with the Sydney LGA being an outlier due to its high crime rate occurs across all crime types. As such the following graphs will not include the Sydney LGA (see discussion for reasoning).
Graph 2: Example Data without Sydney LGA

children.label: Graph 2: Example Data without Sydney LGA

children.value: Whilst this graph here does not display the strongest correlation out of all the relationships assessed in this analysis, it does show the greatest difference in the correlation p value between the dataset with the Sydney LGA and the dataset without the LGA. With the Sydney LGA, the relationship is not statistically signifigant but without the Sydney LGA it is (with an r value of -0.41, suggesting moderate negative correlation).
Graph 3: Example Data of High Correlation

children.label: Graph 3: Example Data of High Correlation

children.value: This graph displays the relationship with the strongest correlation (r = -0.74). This data displays that in greater Sydney, rates of violent crime and the percentage of residents who comeplete year 12 are strongly negatively correlated (as high school completion increases, violent crime decreases).
Graph 3: Example Data of Moderate Correlation

children.label: Graph 3: Example Data of Moderate Correlation

children.value: This graph displays a relationship with moderate correlation (r = 0.40). This data displays that in greater Sydney, rates of drug offences and the rate of unemployment is moderatly positively correlated.
